summary.text: A 71-year-old woman presented with a non-resolving left upper lobe consolidation for which histopathologic confirmation was sought. Under intermittent CT guidance with the patient supine, two passes were made with an 11 cm/18G coaxial core biopsy needle targeting the lesion peripherally and avoiding central bronchiectatic changes. After the second pass the patient coughed and the needle was withdrawn using a water-seal technique to minimise air ingress.

Immediate post-procedural CT revealed a small pneumothorax and minor parenchymal haemorrhage, and the pneumothorax did not require drainage. Five minutes later she developed acute left hemiparesis and facial weakness, while she remained alert with stable vital signs and had minor haemoptysis. She was positioned in the right lateral decubitus position and received 15 L oxygen via non-rebreathe mask.

CT revealed air locules in the subarachnoid space overlying the cerebral convexities confirming cerebral arterial air embolism, with no air in the cardiac chambers, great vessels or thoracic aorta. Subsequent CT angiogram of Circle of Willis showed complete resolution of air bubbles. The following day MRI of the brain showed no infarction but mild cortical signal changes suggestive of transient ischaemia. Only mild residual ataxia persisted after 24 h. Histopathology revealed pulmonary adenocarcinoma.

summary.text: A 71-year-old man with a previous right lower lobectomy underwent CT-guided biopsy of a new right middle lobe non-resolving consolidation. Positioned prone, a single pass using a 6 cm 18-gauge needle was performed. Shortly after, on attempting to roll him onto a trolley, he suffered a self-terminating generalised tonic-clonic seizure. His initial vital signs were stable with saturation of 100% on 15 L oxygen via non-rebreathe mask.

CT imaging revealed small air bubbles within intracranial vessels and within the left ventricle. He regained full consciousness the following day but had residual left-sided weakness. Repeat CT scan showed a reduction in the volume of intracranial gas. He underwent rehabilitation but had some residual left-sided paresis. Histology confirmed pulmonary adenocarcinoma. The consent statement says the patient is deceased.
